**Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) — stock performance and analyst targets (through 16 October 2026).** [[1]]

- MU closed at **$878.84** on 16 October 2026, falling **$52.40, or 5.63%**, during that session. [[2]]
- The stock was down **5.1%** from its **$926.55** close one month earlier, on 16 September 2026. [[3]]
- Over the trailing year, MU rose from **$202.38** on 17 October 2025 to **$878.84** on 16 October 2026, a gain of approximately **334.3%**. [[4]]
- Its trailing-12-month trading range was **$198.47 to $1,213.56**; the 16 October close was roughly **27.6% below** the period high and **342.8% above** the low. [[4]]
- The all-time closing high cited was **$1,213.18 on 25 June 2026**, highlighting that the share price had already pulled back materially from its peak despite the exceptional one-year return. [[5]]

**Analyst price targets.** [[1]]

- The S&P Global-polled consensus was **“Strong Buy”** from **49 analysts**, with an average 12-month target of **$1,561**, implying **77.6% upside** from the $878.84 reference price. [[1]]
- That target distribution was unusually broad: **$361 low**, **$1,550 median**, **$1,561 average**, and **$3,000 high**. [[1]]
- The associated rating mix reported by Investing.com was **45 buys, three holds, and one sell**, reinforcing the positive aggregate stance but also showing that the consensus is not unanimous. [[6]]
- Recent target actions included Bank of America at **$1,550**, KeyBanc at **$1,750**, DBS at **$1,400**, J.P. Morgan at **$1,540**, and D.A. Davidson raising its target from **$2,100 to $3,000**. [[1]]
- A separate 46-analyst MarketBeat aggregation was more conservative, at a **$1,407.88** average target, **$300–$3,000** range, and **60.2%** indicated upside; differences reflect provider coverage and target-update timing. [[7]]

**Bottom line:** MU’s share-price performance has been extraordinary over the past year but volatile, with the latest close materially below its June peak; meanwhile, published analyst aggregates remain decisively constructive, though the **$300–$3,000** target range signals exceptionally high disagreement about the durability and magnitude of future earnings power.
